title: Pork, potatoes, and vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark-green leafy; gravy

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of tender pork, boiled or roasted potatoes, and a mix of vegetables, deliberately excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens. It is served with a savory gravy that adds richness and depth of flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide and is a rich source of protein.
Potatoes are a staple carbohydrate source and can be prepared in over 200 different ways.
Excluding carrots, broccoli, and leafy greens is often due to dietary restrictions or allergies.
Traditional gravy is made from meat stock, flour, and spices, giving it a thick and aromatic consistency.
The dish is commonly served at family meals and festive gatherings in Eastern European cuisines.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑rich carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes supply complex carbs that deliver steady energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both pork and potatoes contain B1, B3, and B6 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: The meal contributes iron, zinc, and potassium, important for blood health and blood‑pressure regulation.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Omitting carrots, broccoli, and leafy greens reduces dietary fiber, which can be beneficial for certain gastrointestinal conditions.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Pork can contain saturated fats; individuals with high cholesterol should moderate portion size.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Although rare, some people may have an allergic reaction to pork proteins.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain added salt; low‑sodium versions are recommended for those with hypertension.

items.title: Lack of fiber
items.content: The absence of high‑fiber vegetables may slow digestion for some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot: place sliced pork alongside potatoes and vegetables, then drizzle with gravy. Garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it (cooled first) in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months.
